result.description:
Based in Noosa, Australia, we've partnered with some of the world's largest corporations in personal care and agriculture to deliver our first-of-a-kind products, and we are now rapidly scaling operations to meet increasing demand.

 

We're seeking an exceptional Aquaculture Consultant (Production Technician) with experience in microalgae cultivation to join our growing production team, focused on the large-scale production of microalgae in our recirculating production facilities. This is a hands-on, science-led role: you'll apply aquaculture and environmental-science expertise to optimise cultivation and downstream processing, develop and refine protocols, and drive data-driven improvements across our operations. Based in Noosa, and working alongside world-leading experts in a purpose-driven, highly motivated team, you'll be supported with on-the-job training to help you become a world leader in the field, with opportunities for rapid career progression.

 

Key responsibilities

Maintain and optimise large-scale microalgae cultures across manual, semi-automated and fully automated systems.
Apply aquaculture and environmental-science principles to evaluate culture health, water quality and growth conditions, and identify solutions for production issues and environmental impacts.
Operate closed-system bioreactors in compliance with internal protocols and specified regulatory standards.
Study, conduct and improve downstream processing activities from harvest through to the final product.
Contribute to the ongoing development, optimisation and scientific documentation of the algae production process.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to improve production efficiency.
Maintain precise, accurate records to support data-driven improvements, regulatory compliance and conservation.
Skills and experience required

A degree in environmental science, marine or aquatic science, aquaculture, bioprocessing, biotechnology or a related field (or equivalent industry experience).
Demonstrated experience in microalgae/seaweed cultivation, aquaculture or large-scale biomanufacturing.
Working knowledge of bioprocessing, downstream processing and quality/record-keeping systems.
A problem-solving, can-do attitude.
Strong communication and reporting skills.
What we offer

A competitive salary of AUD $80,000–$90,000 plus superannuation.
A team-first work environment that supports personal and professional growth.
The opportunity to contribute to meaningful, purpose-driven solutions for some of the world's biggest problems.
A diverse and inclusive workplace, with a commitment to continuous learning and innovation.
Monthly team events.
Our company values

Pioneering: embrace curiosity and innovation.
Collaborative: be transparent, honest, and open to feedback.
Decisive: make bold, data-driven decisions.
Accountable: own your work and results.
Fun: create a workplace where people enjoy their work.

To Apply please navigate to our website and apply via the careers page.
result.title: Aquaculture Consultant (Production Technician)

  Hours:  16 - 38 hours/week, Flexible 

  Salary:   Excellent pay + Travel Allowances + CPD + Benefits 

  Location:  Edgecliff, NSW 

   

  About the company:  

 Our client is a dedicated team of therapists providing comprehensive care and support to children and their families on their therapy journey. Specializing in children aged 0-18, they utilize a holistic and evidence-based approach, working collaboratively with families, educators, and other health professionals to ensure each child flourishes and reaches their full potential. Their services encompass a range of therapeutic interventions, including support for sensory, motor, social, cognitive, and learning difficulties, as well as speech and language development. With a focus on kindness, fairness, optimism, and trust, they strive to empower children, building their confidence, resilience, and independence. Services are offered both in their Edgecliff clinic and through mobile visits to homes, schools, and childcare centers across Sydney. They are committed to providing leading-edge interventions, utilizing the latest assessment tools and high-quality resources. 

   

  About the Role:  

 Our client is looking for an enthusiastic Speech Pathologist   to join their multidisciplinary supportive team. As a Speech Pathologist you will be: 

 
	  Screenings:  This position involves performing individual, observation-based speech and language screenings with preschool and kindergarten children in various settings such as preschools, daycare centers, and schools. The screenings will evaluate age-appropriate speech and language development, with a focus on determining school readiness. The results of these screenings, along with any recommendations, will then be communicated to both the children's families and their educators. 
	  Assessments:  This process involves comprehensive developmental assessments for children, conducted in various settings like clinics, daycare centers, schools, or homes. Evaluations utilize standardized and non-standardized assessments, along with clinical observations. Information gathering includes parent phone consultations, questionnaires for parents and teachers, and review of medical records. Initial assessments last 60-90 minutes, and formal reports with recommendations are prepared within 10 days, shared with relevant parties upon consent. Finally, the assessor collaborates with parents to create individualized goals and provides classroom strategies and resources to educators. 
	  Intervention & Ongoing Care:  Regular review assessments should be conducted to track progress toward established goals. Progress reports should be provided after each assessment and also be made available to parents and educators upon request. Finally, children should be discharged from services once they have achieved their designated goals.

The successful candidate will also maintain technical documentation, deliver user guidance, and work closely with internal teams to ensure reliable, secure and efficient ICT services.   Benefits   Competitive salary package.  Friendly and supportive team environment.  Opportunities for training and career progression.  Exposure to diverse ICT projects and technologies.  Stable full-time role with long-term career opportunities.    Task & responsibilities   Lead and drive IT systems and infrastructure efficiency in the organisation.  Conduct regular system reviews and quality audits to evaluate the performance, reliability and security of ICT systems.  Analyse system performance, identify risks, gaps or areas of non-compliance, and recommend practical solutions to improve efficiency and service quality.  Monitor ICT systems, processes and documentation to ensure compliance with company standards and operational procedures.  Investigate, evaluate and diagnose hardware, software, LAN, WAN, network and connectivity issues in company offices, and provide timely support with resolutions.  Install, configure, maintain, upgrade and troubleshoot computers, operating systems, software applications, printers, networks and cloud-based services.  Develop and deliver technical guidance and user training on software applications, business systems and ICT procedures.  Work closely with staff and management to promote awareness of ICT policies, security practices and quality standards.  Create, review and maintain technical documentation, including user guides, operating procedures, technical specifications and support records.  Provide technical expertise to support system maintenance, infrastructure improvements and the ongoing reliability of business systems.  Collaborate with internal teams and external stakeholders to resolve complex technical issues and improve system performance and customer service.    Qualification & experience      A relevant bachelor’s degree qualification is highly preferred  Minimum 2 years of work experience in a similar role  Excellent troubleshooting and Problem-solving skills  Strong Communication and time management abilities  Support team culture and work collaboratively with colleagues  Strong customer service skills with a proactive and professional approach. result.description:
Your new company  
 You will be joining one of Australia's largest underground mining operations and play a critical role in supporting and improving the operational technology systems that keep the site running safely, reliably and efficiently. 
   
  Your new role  
 We are seeking an experienced Process Control Engineer with strong expertise in Rockwell PLCs, AVEVA Plant SCADA (Citect) and Cicode development to support a range of operational and improvement initiatives across processing and mining operations. 
  Key responsibilities include:  
 
  Supporting and maintaining Rockwell ControlLogix and CompactLogix PLC systems.  
  Developing, supporting and enhancing AVEVA Plant SCADA (Citect) applications.  
  Developing and troubleshooting custom Cicode applications.  
  Investigating and resolving complex PLC, SCADA, instrumentation and communication issues.  
  Supporting commissioning, shutdowns and operational readiness activities.  
  Driving process optimisation, reliability improvements and continuous improvement initiatives.  
  Supporting control system upgrades, modifications and capital projects.  
  Managing change control, documentation and engineering governance requirements.  
 
   
  What you'll need to succeed  
 
  Degree qualification in Electrical, Automation, Control Systems or Mechatronics Engineering.  
  5+ years' experience in Process Control, Automation or Control Systems Engineering.  
  Advanced experience with Rockwell ControlLogix and CompactLogix platforms.  
  Advanced experience with AVEVA Plant SCADA (Citect).  
  Demonstrated experience developing and supporting Cicode applications.  
  Strong PLC programming, commissioning and fault-finding skills.  
  Experience within mining, minerals processing, heavy industrial or manufacturing environments.  
  Strong understanding of industrial communications protocols including Ethernet/IP, Modbus and OPC.  
 
   
  What you'll get in return  
 
  8-12 month contract opportunity.  
  4 days on, 3 days off FIFO roster - 12hr days.  
  Flights provided from Brisbane or Townsville.  
  Opportunity to work on a large-scale mining and processing operation.  
  Exposure to operational technology, automation and continuous improvement projects.  
 
   
  What you need to do now  
 If this sounds like the role for you, apply now or email me on Tillyah.Toamau@hays.com.au for a confidential discussion.  Please  click here  to apply.

Join a High-Performing Distribution Team | LO & LF Operators   
 Looking for your next opportunity with one of the world's leading brands? 
 HOBAN Recruitment is seeking experienced and motivated Warehouse Operators to join a busy-paced, modern Distribution Centre in Melbourne. If you're safety-focused, reliable, and thrive in a high-performance environment apply within!  
 About the Role 
 As a Warehouse Operator, you'll report to your Team Coach and play a key role in ensuring customer orders are picked, processed, and dispatched safely, accurately, and efficiently. 
 Your responsibilities will include: 
 
 Operating LO (Order Picker) and LF forklifts safely and efficiently 
 Picking customer orders using RF scanners 
 Loading and unloading stock 
 Receiving, storing, and replenishing inventory 
 Maintaining high standards of safety, quality, productivity, and accuracy 
 Working collaboratively within a supportive team environment 
 
 What We're Looking For 
 To be successful in this role, you'll have: 
 
 A current LO and/or LF Forklift Licence 
 Previous experience in a warehouse or distribution centre environment 
 Experience using RF scanning equipment 
 Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy 
 A positive attitude and excellent teamwork skills 
 A strong commitment to workplace health and safety 
 The ability to work in a busy-paced, physically active environment 
 
 What's on Offer 
 
 Work with a globally recognised industry leader 
 Competitive hourly rates with casual loading 
 Weekly pay 
 Full training and ongoing support 
 A safe, inclusive, and supportive workplace 
 Career development and progression opportunities 
 Potential for long-term and permanent employment based on performance 
 
 Pre-Employment Requirements 
 Successful applicants will be required to complete: 
 
 Drug and Alcohol Screening 
 National Police Check 
 
 Apply Now 
 Apply today for immediate consideration and start your journey with HOBAN Recruitment. 

 At HOBAN we encourage applications from people with disability, people from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds, people of all genders, LGBTI people, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. 
 We provide reasonable adjustments; including alternate formats to the recruitment process for individuals with disability. If you require an adjustment to be made during the recruitment process, please email our Adjustments Coordinator at  adjustments@hoban.com.au  or visit  hoban.com.au/adjustments  for additional contact details.  Please  click here  to apply.
